subject: physics
content: Which of the following statement is not true about stopping potential ?

options.content: It depends upon frequency of the incident light.

It is <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.566ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="3.267ex" height="2.262ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -750 1444 1000" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mn"><use data-c="31" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-31"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(500,0)"><use data-c="2F" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2F"></use></g><g data-mml-node="TeXAtom" data-mjx-texclass="ORD" transform="translate(1000,0)"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="65" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-65"></use></g></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> times the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted.
It increases with increase in intensity of the incident light.
It depends on the nature of emitter material.

explanation: Stopping potential is independent of intensity of light. It depends on frequency of light.
